mainTopic: Seizing a dead debtor's property from the heirs: רבי טרפון versus רבי עקיבא, reversing court rulings, and real cases of seizure
overview: The גמרא continues the משנה's dispute between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא about a man who dies owing money and leaves property to his heirs. First it learns that even for רבי עקיבא, grabbing the property works if it was done while the debtor was still alive. Then it asks where the produce must be for רבי טרפון's rule that whoever grabs first wins. רב and שמואל say only in רשות הרבים; רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say even in a סימטא. Next comes a story: judges ruled like רבי טרפון, ריש לקיש reversed it, and רבי יוחנן objected. The גמרא gives three ways to explain their argument, while both sides agree that a mistake in a matter found in the משנה is reversed. More real cases follow: רבי יוחנן's relatives and an orphans' cow, רב נחמן believing a creditor about an ox because of a מגו, and רבי אבא protesting a ruling that favored the נשיא's household. The amud ends as רב פפא and רב הונא object to an agent who seized a dead man's boat at the expense of other creditors. רבי יוחנן's rule about that is completed on the next amud.

steps.title: Does grabbing never work for רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to רבי עקיבא, a creditor's seizing of property is never effective.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, does seizing the property not help at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי עקיבא's opinion. Does his view mean that grabbing the property never helps a creditor?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives the dead man's property to the heirs and not to the creditor. That seems to mean a creditor who grabs it gains nothing. The גמרא wants to know whether this is always true.

keyTerms.meaning: Seizing or grabbing property to collect what you are owed

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva,
does seizing not help at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, תְּפִיסָה לָא מַהְנְיָא כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the משנה's dispute between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי עקיבא allows seizure to be effective in any case

steps.title: Seizing works if done while the debtor was alive
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that even רבי עקיבא agrees seizure works if it was done during the debtor's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: That is, seizure works when the creditor seized the property while the man was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Grabbing does work for רבי עקיבא, but only if it happened while the debtor was still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the man dies, his property passes to the heirs, so grabbing it after death is too late. A grab made while he was alive came before the heirs had any rights, so it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is when... (this adds a condition)

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:
And that is when he seized it while the man was alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: וְהוּא שֶׁתָּפַס מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seizure works for רבי עקיבא only if it was done during the debtor's lifetime
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, grabbing a debtor's property works only if it was done before he died. After death, the property belongs to the heirs.

steps.title: Where must the produce be for רבי טרפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the produce must be lying for רבי טרפון's rule that whoever grabs first acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי טרפון, where was the produce placed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי טרפון's view that whoever grabs the produce first gets it. It asks where that produce has to be lying for the rule to apply. This sets up the dispute in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location matters because in some places the heirs automatically acquire whatever is lying there. If they already own it, nobody else can grab it.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Tarfon,
where were they placed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, דְּמַנְּחִי הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי עקיבא to רבי טרפון
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location of the produce where רבי טרפון's rule of 'whoever grabs first acquires it' applies

steps.title: רב and שמואל: only in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל say the rule applies only to produce piled in רשות הרבים, not produce in a סימטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: That is when the produce is piled and lying in רשות הרבים. But if it is in a סימטא, the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer is that whoever grabs first wins only when the produce is lying in a public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Acquiring something is not possible in רשות הרבים, so the heirs have not yet acquired the produce there, and anyone can grab it. A סימטא is a place where acquiring does work, so the heirs acquire the produce right away and no one else can take it.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, such as a main street
An alley beside the public domain that few people use

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
And that is when they are piled and lying in the public domain,
but in an alley, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: וְהוּא שֶׁצְּבוּרִין וּמוּנָּחִין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule applies only in רשות הרבים, not in a סימטא

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: even in an alley
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say that whoever grabs first acquires the produce even when it is in a סימטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: Even in a סימטא.
steps.whatsHappening: A second pair of אמוראים disagrees with רב and שמואל. They hold that for רבי טרפון, grabbing first works even in an alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, a סימטא does not stop the grabber. This makes רבי טרפון's rule apply in more cases than רב and שמואל allowed.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, who both say:
Even in an alley.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: אֲפִילּוּ בְּסִימְטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule applies even in a סימטא
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי טרפון, whoever grabs the produce first wins. רב and שמואל say this applies only in רשות הרבים. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say it applies even in a סימטא.

steps.title: Judges ruled like רבי טרפון and ריש לקיש reversed it
steps.stepSummary: In a real case, judges ruled like רבי טרפון, and ריש לקיש overturned their decision.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some judges ruled like רבי טרפון, and ריש לקיש reversed their ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real court case. The judges followed רבי טרפון, and ריש לקיש undid their decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש did not accept the ruling because the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא. Reversing it meant giving the property back to the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: He reversed it / sent it back

phrases.english: Judges ruled in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon,
and Reish Lakish reversed their action.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּן דַּיָּינֵי כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from theory to a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש reversed a court ruling that followed רבי טרפון

steps.title: רבי יוחנן objects to the reversal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells ריש לקיש that he treated the case as if it were a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: You acted as one does with a matter of Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן criticizes ריש לקיש. He says ריש לקיש reversed the ruling as if the judges had gone against an explicit Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a court rules against a clear Torah law, its ruling must be fixed. רבי יוחנן's point is that this case was not that kind of mistake, so the ruling should not have been undone.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a matter of Torah law

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
You acted as with a matter of Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עָשִׂיתָ כְּשֶׁל תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds critically to ריש לקיש's action in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reversal of the judges' ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a mistake against Torah law requires reversing a ruling, and this case was not that kind of mistake

steps.title: Is their dispute about a mistake in a משנה ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן disagree about whether a judge who erred in a matter found in the משנה has his ruling reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree about this? One Sage holds that if a judge erred in a matter found in the משנה, the ruling is reversed. The other holds that if he erred in a matter found in the משנה, the ruling is not reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a suggestion to explain the disagreement between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן. It is setting up the next move, where this suggestion will be examined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion has two sides. ריש לקיש would hold that a mistake in a matter found in the משנה is reversed, which is why he undid the judges' ruling. רבי יוחנן would hold that such a mistake is not reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (this opens a suggestion)
Made a mistake in a matter found in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' only introduces a suggestion, not a conclusion. The גמרא often goes on to reject a לימא suggestion, so do not treat it as the final answer yet.

phrases.english: Shall we say they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר טָעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה חוֹזֵר,
phrases.english: that one Sage holds that if one erred in a matter of the Mishnah, it is reversed,
phrases.notes: This 'מר' is ריש לקיש, who reversed the ruling.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר טָעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר?
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that if one erred in a matter of the Mishnah, it is not reversed?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the disagreement shown in steps 6-7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute is about reversing a judge's mistake in a matter found in the משנה
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a court's mistaken ruling can be undone is an important question for how בתי דין work in practice.

steps.title: Everyone agrees a mistake in a משנה is reversed; the argument is about following רבי עקיבא against his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 8. Both sides agree that a mistake in a משנה-level matter is reversed. They argue about whether we follow רבי עקיבא even when he disagrees with his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that if a judge made a mistake in a matter found in the משנה, his ruling is reversed. Here they argue about this: one master holds that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא against his colleague but not against his teacher. The other master holds that the הלכה follows him even against his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to the suggestion in Step 8. It gives a different reason why רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a clear mistake in a משנה must be reversed. The real question is whether the judges actually made a mistake. רבי יוחנן holds that we do not follow רבי עקיבא against his teacher רבי טרפון, so ruling like רבי טרפון was no mistake. ריש לקיש holds that we follow רבי עקיבא even against his teacher, so the judges did make a mistake and their ruling is reversed.
steps.confusionAlert: The text only says 'one master… the other master.' From the case, the one who follows רבי עקיבא only against a colleague is רבי יוחנן. The one who follows him even against his teacher is ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
that if a judge erred in a matter found in the משנה, his ruling is reversed.
And here they disagree about this:
One master holds the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא
against his colleague, but not against his teacher,
phrases.notes: The idea is that רבי טרפון was רבי עקיבא's teacher, so here we would not follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: and the other master holds the הלכה follows him even against his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא טָעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested explanation in Step 8 and replaces it with a new point of disagreement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two disagree about reversing a mistake in a משנה-level matter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both actually agree on that rule. The argument can instead be about how far the principle of following רבי עקיבא reaches.

steps.title: Or: they argue whether רבי טרפון was רבי עקיבא's teacher or his colleague
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: both agree we follow רבי עקיבא only against a colleague. They argue about whether רבי טרפון was his teacher or his colleague.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: everyone agrees the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא against his colleague but not against his teacher. Here they argue about this: one master holds רבי טרפון was his teacher, and the other master holds he was his colleague.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible way to explain the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rule itself is agreed on. The argument becomes a question of fact about the relationship between the two sages. If רבי טרפון was the teacher (רבי יוחנן), the judges did not err. If he was a colleague (ריש לקיש), the judges erred and are reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another explanation)

phrases.english: And if you want, say instead:
everyone agrees the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא
against his colleague but not against his teacher.
And here they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן רַבּוֹ הֲוָה,
phrases.english: one master holds רבי טרפון was his teacher,
and the other master holds he was his colleague.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וְלֹא מֵרַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the rule from Step 9 as agreed by both, and moves the disagreement to a question of fact.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument from a legal principle to a factual question about the relationship between the sages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two argue about how far the rule of following רבי עקיבא reaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: They may agree on the rule and argue only about whether רבי טרפון was רבי עקיבא's teacher.

steps.title: Or: they argue whether the rule was stated as firm הלכה or only as a leaning
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: both agree רבי טרפון was a colleague. They argue about whether following רבי עקיבא was said as firm הלכה or only as 'we lean toward' (מטין).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: everyone agrees he was his colleague. Here they argue about this: one master holds it was stated as 'הלכה,' and the other master holds it was stated as 'we lean toward it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third possible way to explain the argument, this time about how strongly the rule was stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule was said as firm הלכה (ריש לקיש), going against it is a real mistake, so the ruling is reversed. If it was only said as 'מטין,' a leaning (רבי יוחנן), it was never set firmly. Judges who ruled the other way are then not reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: We lean toward (a softer guideline, not firm הלכה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to explain the argument, and both sides always agree that a clear mistake in a משנה is reversed. They argue about (1) following רבי עקיבא against a teacher, (2) whether רבי טרפון was his teacher, or (3) whether the rule was firm הלכה or only מטין.

phrases.english: And if you want, say instead:
everyone agrees he was his colleague,
and here they disagree about this:
one master holds 'הלכה' was stated,
and the other master holds 'we lean toward it' was stated.
phrases.notes: 'Leaning toward' means we follow רבי עקיבא from the start, but it was never set as a firm rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חֲבֵירוֹ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that רבי טרפון was a colleague and moves the argument to how strongly the rule was stated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to the strength of the rule (firm הלכה versus a leaning).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They argue about whether רבי טרפון was a teacher or a colleague.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if all agree he was a colleague, they can argue about whether the rule was firm הלכה or only מטין.

steps.title: The story of the orphans' cow seized from an alley
steps.stepSummary: Relatives of רבי יוחנן seized an orphans' cow from a סימטא. רבי יוחנן approved, ריש לקיש told them to return it, and רבי יוחנן said he could not overrule an equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Relatives of רבי יוחנן seized a cow belonging to orphans from an alley. They came before רבי יוחנן, and he said to them: you seized it properly. They came before רבי שמעון בן לקיש, and he said to them: go, return it. They came back before רבי יוחנן. He said to them: what can I do? The one who is my equal disagrees with me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that shows the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agreed in Step 5 that according to רבי טרפון, grabbing in a סימטא works. רבי יוחנן rules like רבי טרפון, so his relatives may keep the cow. ריש לקיש rules like רבי עקיבא, as in Step 6, and orders it returned. רבי יוחנן does not force his ruling, because ריש לקיש is his equal in stature.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who is equal to me

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when two equal sages disagree, one cannot simply override the other's ruling.

phrases.english: Relatives of רבי יוחנן
seized a cow belonging to orphans from an alley.
They came before רבי יוחנן,
he said to them: you seized it properly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: They came before רבי שמעון בן לקיש,
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש, written out with his full name.

phrases.english: he said to them: go, return it.
They came before רבי יוחנן again.
He said to them: what can I do?
For the one who is my equal disagrees with me.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן תְּפוּס פָּרָה דְיַתְמֵי מִסִּימְטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case showing the רבי יוחנן–ריש לקיש dispute (Steps 6-7) over following רבי טרפון, here with a seizure in a סימטא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן ruled that seizing from orphans in a סימטא is valid. ריש לקיש ordered the cow returned, and רבי יוחנן did not overrule an equal.

steps.title: A creditor seizes an ox from the orphans' herdsman
steps.stepSummary: A creditor took an ox from the herdsman who cared for orphans' cattle. The creditor says he took it while the debtor was alive. The herdsman says it was taken after the debtor died. They bring the case to רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a herdsman who looked after orphans' cattle, and someone took an ox from him. The creditor said: 'I took it while the father was still alive.' The herdsman said: 'He took it after the father died.' They came to רב נחמן to decide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story and sets up a dispute about timing. The ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing is the whole case. Seizing before the debtor died counts even according to רבי עקיבא. Seizing from orphans after death does not count according to him. So each side claims the timing that helps him.

keyTerms.meaning: Herdsman, someone who looks after cattle
Orphans (here, the heirs of the dead debtor)
Creditor, the one who is owed money

phrases.english: There was a certain herdsman of orphans
from whom they seized an ox.
The creditor said:
I seized it during his lifetime.
phrases.notes: He means while the orphans' father, who owed him money, was still alive.

phrases.english: And the herdsman said:
He seized it after the death.
They came before רב נחמן.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בַּקָּרָא דְיַתְמֵי דְּתָפְסִי תּוֹרָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical case about seizing orphans' movable property. It builds on the earlier discussion of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: the creditor and the herdsman disagree about whether the ox was seized before or after the debtor's death.

steps.title: רב נחמן believes the creditor because of a מגו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks the herdsman for witnesses to the seizure, and he has none. So the creditor is believed. He could have claimed he bought the ox, so he can also claim he seized it during the debtor's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן asked the herdsman: 'Do you have witnesses that he took it from you?' He said: 'No.' רב נחמן said: 'Since the creditor could have said, "I bought it, and that is why it is in my hands," he can also say, "I took it while the father was alive."'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן decides the case for the creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one saw the creditor take the ox, so all we know is that it is now in his hands. He could have won by simply saying 'I bought it.' So we also believe the weaker claim he actually made, that he seized it while the debtor was alive.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': if he could have won with a stronger claim, we believe the claim he made
'It was bought and is in my hand,' a claim of purchase

steps.whatToRemember: Possession plus no witnesses lets the holder use a מגו: he could have said 'I bought it,' so he is believed that he seized it in time.
steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses being asked about are witnesses to the seizure itself. If witnesses saw the creditor grab the ox, he could no longer claim he bought it. Then the מגו would fall away.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you have witnesses
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is speaking to the herdsman.

phrases.english: that he seized it?
He said to him: No.
He said to him: Since he could say
'It was bought and is in my hand,'
he can also say
'I seized it during his lifetime.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִית לְךָ סָהֲדֵי דְּתַפְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's ruling on the case set up in Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The creditor is believed because of a מגו. He could have claimed he bought the ox.

steps.title: Challenge: wandering animals do not prove ownership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's ruling with ריש לקיש's rule that animals that roam give no presumption of ownership. If so, the 'I bought it' claim should not work, and the מגו falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ריש לקיש said that animals that wander around do not give their holder a presumption of ownership!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the basis of רב נחמן's מגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגו works only if holding the ox would let the creditor say 'I bought it.' But animals wander from place to place, so having one does not show you own it. Then the creditor's possession proves nothing, and his claim should not be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't [so-and-so] say...', the opening of a challenge
Animals that roam, such as sheep and cattle
Presumption of ownership based on possession

phrases.english: But didn't ריש לקיש say:
Roaming animals have no presumption of ownership!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הַגּוֹדְרוֹת אֵין לָהֶן חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מגו used in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's מגו that the creditor could have said 'I bought it.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holding an animal does not show ownership, so the 'I bought it' claim, and the מגו built on it, should fail.

steps.title: An ox is different because it is given to a shepherd
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an ox is unlike other animals. It is handed over to a shepherd who watches it, so it does not wander. Holding an ox therefore does show ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox is different, because it is handed over to a shepherd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן's ruling against the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule is based on animals wandering off on their own. An ox is kept under a shepherd's care, so it does not stray into someone else's hands. Holding it is meaningful, and the מגו stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is different,' a way of answering by making a distinction

phrases.english: An ox is different,
since it is handed over to a shepherd.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי תּוֹרָא דִּמְסִירָה לְרוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: an ox is a special case within ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All animals, oxen included, give no presumption of ownership, so the מגו fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: An ox is watched by a shepherd and does not wander, so holding it shows ownership and the מגו works.

steps.title: The נשיא's household seizes an orphans' maidservant
steps.stepSummary: Members of the נשיא's household seized a maidservant belonging to orphans in an alleyway. רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי יצחק נפחא were sitting as judges, with רבי אבא beside them. The seizure was approved: 'You seized her properly.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The household of the נשיא grabbed a maidservant who belonged to orphans, in an alleyway. רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי יצחק נפחא were sitting, and רבי אבא sat with them. He said to them: 'You seized her properly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another case of seizing orphans' property after the father died. It reports a ruling approving the seizure, which is challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the cow case from Step 12: property of orphans grabbed in an alleyway. Approving the seizure fits רבי טרפון's view, which lets a creditor collect from orphans' movable property after death.

keyTerms.meaning: The household of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish community in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: The household of the נשיא seized
a maidservant of orphans from an alleyway.
רבי אבהו was sitting
and רבי חנינא בר פפי
and רבי יצחק נפחא,
and רבי אבא was sitting with them.
He said to them: You seized her properly.
phrases.notes: The text doesn't name the speaker. It seems to be one of the judges, speaking to the נשיא's household.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה תְּפוּס אַמְתָא דְיַתְמֵי מִסִּימְטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case parallel to the orphans' cow in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judges approve the seizure of the orphans' maidservant.

steps.title: רבי אבא protests: the הלכה does not follow רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא accuses the judges of flattering the נשיא's household. He reminds them that judges once ruled like רבי טרפון and ריש לקיש reversed their ruling. So the seizure should not stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to them: 'Just because they are the נשיא's household, you flatter them? Judges once ruled like רבי טרפון, and ריש לקיש reversed what they did!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges the approval given in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Approving the seizure follows רבי טרפון. But ריש לקיש already reversed a ruling based on רבי טרפון, which shows the הלכה is like רבי עקיבא. So seizing orphans' property after death does not work, even for important people.

keyTerms.meaning: An action or ruling that was carried out

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to Steps 6 to 11. The ruling against רבי טרפון is strong enough that a judge's decision following him gets reversed, even when powerful people benefit.

phrases.english: רבי אבא said to them:
Because they are the household of the נשיא
will you flatter them?
But judges once ruled like רבי טרפון,
and ריש לקיש reversed their action.
phrases.notes: This is the story from Step 6, where judges ruled like רבי טרפון and ריש לקיש cancelled their ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אַבָּא: מִשּׁוּם דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה נִינְהוּ מְחַנְּפִיתוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the approval in Step 17 by pointing to the case in Step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That ruling follows רבי טרפון. ריש לקיש already reversed a ruling like that, so this one is a mistake and looks like favoritism.

steps.title: יימר בר חשו has his agent seize a dead debtor's boat
steps.stepSummary: A man owed יימר בר חשו money, then died and left a boat. יימר told his agent to seize the boat for him, and the agent did.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man owed יימר בר חשו money. The man died and left a boat. יימר said to his agent: 'Go, grab it for me.' He went and grabbed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about seizing a dead debtor's property, this time through an agent. The objection comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that someone else does the seizing for the creditor. This sets up the question of whether an agent can seize for a creditor when other people are hurt by it.

phrases.english: יימר בר חשו

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי בְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא,
phrases.english: was owed money by a certain man.
He died and left a boat.
He said to his agent:
Go, seize it for me.
He went and seized it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵימַר בַּר חָשׁוּ הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי בְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about seizing a dead debtor's movable property, now done by an agent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: an agent seizes a dead debtor's boat for the creditor.

steps.title: רב פפא and רב הונא object: seizing at others' expense
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע meet the agent. They tell him he is seizing for a creditor in a way that causes loss to others. They begin quoting רבי יוחנן's rule about this, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, met him. They said: 'You are seizing for a creditor in a case where it causes loss to others. And רבי יוחנן said: One who seizes for a creditor in a case where it causes loss to others...'
steps.whatsHappening: Two rabbis object to the agent's seizure. They quote רבי יוחנן, whose ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debtor owed money to other people too. By grabbing the boat for one creditor, the agent takes away what the others could collect. רבי יוחנן's rule about this kind of seizure is about to be given.

keyTerms.meaning: They met him, came across him
Seizing on behalf of a creditor
Causing a loss to other people

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off in the middle of רבי יוחנן's statement. His actual ruling comes at the start of the next amud, so don't look for the conclusion here.

phrases.english: רב פפא met him
together with רב הונא, son of רב יהושע.
They said to him:
You are seizing for a creditor
in a case where it causes loss to others.
And רבי יוחנן said:
One who seizes for a creditor
in a case where it causes loss to others

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ תּוֹפֵס לְבַעַל חוֹב בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁחָב לַאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the agent's seizure described in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The agent's seizure of the boat for יימר בר חשו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seizing for one creditor takes away from the debtor's other creditors. רבי יוחנן has a rule about seizing in such a case, and it continues on the next amud.
